# llms.txt — @fams/skeleton-kit export index (hand-authored: this package's
# showcase coverage is none and its JSDoc is prose, not fixture-shaped, so
# cheap auto-generation (see scripts/build-llms.mjs, "generated" mode) reads
# worse than a human summary here — see the task brief's allowance for
# hand-written llms.txt "where generation is disproportionate"). Every
# current barrel export symbol name must appear somewhere below as a whole
# word; `pnpm build:llms -- --check` (wired into `pnpm lint`) enforces it —
# a new export with no matching mention here fails the gate.
# format: Symbol(s) :: purpose :: key signature/props :: file

createFamsApp :: The one boot call — wires TanStack Router (per-module lazy code-splitting), TanStack Query defaults, theming bootstrap (data-theme/data-tenant), and a root error boundary into a running app. :: createFamsApp(config: FamsAppConfig) → FamsApp :: src/createFamsApp.tsx
FamsModule, NavEntry, ModuleRouteLoader :: The locked module contract every consuming app implements — one entry per app module (route loader + nav metadata). :: FamsModule { id, nav?: NavEntry, routes: ModuleRouteLoader }, NavEntry { label, icon?, path }, ModuleRouteLoader = () => Promise<...> :: src/types.ts
buildRouter, DefaultRouteErrorComponent, BuildRouterOptions, FamsRouter, ShellComponentProps :: Assembles the TanStack Router instance from the registered FamsModules, with a default route-error fallback. `BuildRouterOptions.shellComponent` (prop shape `ShellComponentProps`) lets a caller override the root-route chrome rendered around `<Outlet/>` — defaults to this package's own `AppShell` (product-agnostic; `@fams/v5-kit`'s `V5AppShell` is the v5-tier override). :: buildRouter(options: BuildRouterOptions) → FamsRouter; ShellComponentProps { modules, brandLabel? } :: src/router.tsx
withNavRouteDriftGuard, withAdditionalRouteDriftGuard :: Dev-only loud guards used internally by `buildRouter` that assert a route's path matches its `createLazyRoute(id)` id — the first for a module's primary route (`navEntry.path`), the second (generalized, takes `moduleId` + a `ModuleRouteEntry`) for each `additionalRoutes[]` entry. :: withNavRouteDriftGuard(module: FamsModule) → ModuleRouteLoader; withAdditionalRouteDriftGuard(moduleId: string, entry: ModuleRouteEntry) → ModuleRouteLoader :: src/router.tsx
ModuleRouteEntry, ModuleSearchValidator :: v1.1 additive types for the module contract. `ModuleRouteEntry` is one additional route beyond a module's primary `navEntry.path` (its own `path`, its own independently-lazy-loaded `routes`, optional `validateSearch`) — used via `FamsModule.additionalRoutes[]`, e.g. a `/$id` detail view alongside a list, each code-split into its own chunk. `ModuleSearchValidator<TSearch>` types the eager search-param validator function an author writes for `FamsModule.validateSearch` / `ModuleRouteEntry.validateSearch` (erased to TanStack's `AnyValidator` once stored on the contract). :: ModuleRouteEntry { path, routes: ModuleRouteLoader, validateSearch?: AnyValidator }; ModuleSearchValidator<TSearch = Record<string, unknown>> = Validator<Record<string, unknown>, TSearch> :: src/types.ts
AppShell, deriveNavEntries, AppShellProps, DerivedNavItem :: The generic app chrome shell + the pure function that turns registered modules into nav items (active-state, ordering). :: AppShellProps { modules, activePath, … }, deriveNavEntries(modules) → DerivedNavItem[] :: src/shell.tsx
createFamsQueryClient, queryClassOptions, gcTimeForClass, DEFAULT_GC_TIMES, QueryClass, QueryConfig :: TanStack Query client factory with the three-class gcTime model (`static`/`session`/`volatile`) so a module never hand-tunes cache lifetime per query. :: QueryClass = 'static' | 'session' | 'volatile'; gcTimeForClass(cls: QueryClass) → number :: src/query.ts
useTheme, setTheme, getTheme, toggleTheme, bootstrapTheme, resolveInitialTheme, ThemeMode, ThemeBootstrapConfig, DefaultThemeMode :: Theming bootstrap — resolves/sets `data-theme` on first load (OS preference → stored override) and exposes a live hook + imperative setters. `defaultThemeMode` ('force' default | 'respect-stored') controls whether `defaultTheme` overrides a stored choice — 'force' is today's behavior, pending a product decision (BACKLOG.md). :: ThemeMode = 'light' | 'dark'; useTheme() → ThemeMode; setTheme(mode: ThemeMode); resolveInitialTheme(defaultTheme?, mode?: DefaultThemeMode) :: src/theming.ts
RootErrorBoundary, DefaultErrorFallback, ErrorFallbackProps :: Root-level React error boundary with a default fallback UI; app can swap in its own via `ErrorFallbackProps`. :: ErrorFallbackProps { error, resetErrorBoundary } :: src/error-boundary.tsx
